guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul / Jackson Randy Rhoads model / Gibson Les Paul (Wylde "Bullseye")
guitar.evidence: Randy Rhoads played Gibson Les Pauls and the Karl Sandoval-built polka-dot V (later Jackson's signature Randy Rhoads model) on "Crazy Train"/"Mr. Crowley"; Zakk Wylde's bullseye Gibson Les Paul is iconic for "Bark at the Moon"-era and beyond.
guitar.notes: Was unknown despite Ozzy's guitarists being among the most documented in metal history; filled with high confidence.

tone.target: bright 80s metal crunch with nasal lead bite
tone.profile: bright 80s metal crunch with nasal lead bite
tone.summary: A tight, high-gain signal chain utilizing a Marshall-style preamp (UK SLP) for the core rhythm tone, enhanced with an OD boost for attack, followed by a wah filter and controlled ambience.

rig.name: Ozzy Osbourne - Bark at the Moon - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Tighten up the aggressive metal tone and eliminate hum.
Provide aggressive note attack and mid-range punch for palm mutes.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to simulate a tight, biting boost characteristic of 80s metal leads.

alternatives.reason: Slightly warmer, but still provides necessary bite.

blocks.purpose: Establish the core high-gain crunch and sustain required for 80s metal.
blocks.gap: Using a general Distortion model to achieve the JCM800/Marshall saturation without excessive low end.

alternatives.reason: Could provide more aggressive grit, but might be too harsh.

blocks.purpose: Provide the explicit wah lead color and vocal bite required for solos.
Simulate the classic Marshall/JCM800 tone with pronounced mids and bite.
Provide the classic British 4x12 cabinet sound.
Further emphasize the mid-range bite and control excessive low end.
blocks.gap: Used to manually sculpt the frequency response, ensuring mids are forward without muddying the bass.

blocks.purpose: Optional subtle thickening for leads (kept off by default to avoid wash).
blocks.gap: The Chorus is kept inactive/low depth as per 'avoid chorus wash' instruction, but included for completeness.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle rhythmic depth to the rhythm parts.
blocks.gap: A moderate delay is used for structural support without distracting from the aggressive tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide a natural sense of space without sounding overly wet or muddy.
blocks.gap: A subtle Room reverb is preferred over Plate/Spring to maintain the aggressive, dry feel of 80s metal.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for authentic 80s British crunch.

proposals.reason: Enhance the classic Marshall/JCM800 sound and mid-range bite.
